summary: Manufacturer-coverage quantity (5 of the 25 pilot work items: joint compound, primer, wall paint, ceiling paint, curing compound) is wrong or non-deterministic. (a) _consumption_qty takes the lowest consumption_id among ALL products that share the spec_key (line 886) but the line is then priced with the MEDIAN price of all those products, so one product's spread rate is multiplied by another product's price; (b) coverage_unit_id is never converted to the work item's output unit (line 890 uses cov as if it were already per output unit); (c) coverage_qty = 0 or coats = 0 raises decimal.DivisionByZero (schema allows both, schema 228/233); (d) film_thickness / substrate_condition / application_method / conditions on the consumption row are never matched to anything on the component, so two rows for different film thickness are 'alternatives' picked by hash order; (e) products that are flagged/rejected are included in the product set (lines 879-882).
reproduction:
db = S.real_db(); S.add_source(db)
S.add_product(db,'TEST-PRD-PA','prm_pva_5',5,'GAL_US','A','A-1'); S.add_obs(db,'TEST-OBS-PA','TEST-PRD-PA','100',5,'GAL_US')   # $20/gal
S.add_product(db,'TEST-PRD-PB','prm_pva_5',5,'GAL_US','B','B-1'); S.add_obs(db,'TEST-OBS-PB','TEST-PRD-PB','200',5,'GAL_US')   # $40/gal
S.add_labor_actual(db,'TEST-LRT-PNT','TR-PNT',40); S.set_crew(db,'CRW-PNT',8,[('labor','TR-PNT',2,False)])
S.set_productivity(db,'WI-PNT-001',2,8,2000); S.set_waste(db,'WI-PNT-001',{'CAT-PNT-PRM':(0.0,'t')})
# two product_consumption rows (application='new_drywall_primer', coats=1, coverage_unit SF): TEST-CON-A -> product A 400 SF/gal, TEST-CON-B -> product B 200 SF/gal
# true cost per SF: A 0.05, B 0.20, median 0.125.  Engine extended_cost = 0.0750 ; after renaming the ids so that B's row sorts first = 0.1500.
# same data with coverage_unit_id='SY' (400 SY/gal) on this SF work item: material qty 0.0025 (correct 0.0225).  coverage_qty=0 or coats=0: decimal.DivisionByZero.
suggested_fix: Pair coverage with the same product that is priced: per product compute cost per output unit = (price per pack / pack content) x (product units per output unit) and take the median of THOSE; require exactly one usable consumption row per (product, application) or add film_thickness/conditions selectors on the component and fail when ambiguous; convert coverage_unit_id to wi.output_unit_id with Units.factor; add CHECK (coverage_qty > 0 AND coats > 0 AND per_qty > 0) on product_consumption; filter products through the same usability test as observations; add tests (none exist for this path).

summary: Strict-mode leak. methodology.md section 1 promises 'flagged and rejected records are never used by any calculation', but review_status is only honoured for the row that is passed through _usable() (observations, labor/burden/equipment rates, productivity, consumption). It is ignored for: sources (a rejected source's rows stay usable), crews, indices (data/csv/indices.csv already contains ECICONWAG with review_status=flagged by reviewer F2; a flagged series with validated values still adjusts prices), approved assumptions (assumptions.review_status), and products (only 'rejected' is excluded at line 250; pinned products at 246 are not checked at all, so unreviewed and flagged products are priced in strict/validated mode).
reproduction:
for s in db['sources']: s['review_status'] = 'rejected'          # source with all inputs
print(run(db).status, run(db).run['direct_cost_total'])          # complete 0.997875  (expected: incomplete)
# crew review_status='rejected' -> complete ; product review_status='flagged' or 'unreviewed' -> complete 0.997875
# index series review_status='flagged' (validated values) with time_index_id=... -> complete, TIME_INDEXED_PRICE
# approved assumption with review_status='rejected' -> complete
suggested_fix: One helper usable(row, params) applied to every referenced table (sources, products, crews, indices, assumptions, factors, work items); in strict mode require validated for products/crews/indices as well; a record whose source is flagged/rejected is unusable; add a test per table.

line: 311-345 (calculation_runs/lines, no trigger; line 342 ON DELETE CASCADE; cr_complete_chk 336)
summary: Calculation records are not protected. calculation_runs and calculation_run_lines have no append-only trigger, lines cascade-delete with their run, and cr_complete_chk only requires a non-null total and an empty missing_inputs array: an incomplete run can be rewritten into a 'complete' run with an invented total and no lines, and formula/inputs/parameters/calc_version of an existing run can be edited. This violates rule 9 (calculation records link to inputs, formula and version; history never overwritten).
reproduction:
-- PostgreSQL, data/csv loaded
update costdb.calculation_runs set status='complete', direct_cost_total=123.45, missing_inputs='[]' where run_id=(select run_id from costdb.calculation_runs limit 1);   -- UPDATE 1
update costdb.calculation_run_lines set formula='x', inputs='[]'::jsonb, extended_cost=1 where line_no=1;                                                              -- UPDATE
delete from costdb.calculation_runs where run_id=(select run_id from costdb.calculation_runs limit 1);                                                                -- DELETE 1, 4 lines cascade
suggested_fix: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE triggers on both tables (only review_status/reviewed_*/notes updatable); replace ON DELETE CASCADE with RESTRICT; deferred constraint trigger: a 'complete' run must have >= 1 line and direct_cost_total equal to the sum of its component lines; NOT NULL calc_version and code_ref for non-test runs.

summary: Regression introduced by the F2 enum change: reuse_status 'licence_required' (now used by the three CSI sources) is blocked nowhere. NO_DATA_USE = ('prohibited','restricted_no_storage') so a licence_required source is a usable calculation input; validate.py raises SRC_PROHIBITED_IN_USE only for prohibited/restricted_no_storage and SRC_PROHIBITED_VALIDATED only for 'prohibited' (a validated restricted_no_storage or licence_required source is accepted); the importer accepts licence_required with no warning, and accepts 'prohibited' sources with capture_method=manual_browser (validate.py then flags every such row as an error and the engine ignores it, so the importer admits rows that the rest of the system rejects).
reproduction:
for s in db['sources']:
    if s['source_id'] == S.SRC: s['reuse_status'] = 'licence_required'
run(db).status                                   # complete 0.997875 ; validate(db, production=False) -> no issue
# source 'restricted_no_storage' + review_status='validated' -> no SRC_PROHIBITED_VALIDATED
suggested_fix: Define the restricted-status sets once (e.g. costdb/enums.py) and import them in calc, validate, importer and tests; decide explicitly whether licence_required means 'no data use until licence recorded'; make the importer refuse prohibited/restricted_no_storage regardless of capture_method.

summary: Region, condition and quantity factor rows never pass through _usable(): the factor's source (prohibited, restricted_no_storage, synthetic fixture, flagged) is not checked. A factor from a prohibited source is applied in a strict run.
reproduction:
S.add_source(db, 'SRC-PROH', method='fetched_primary', review='validated', reuse='prohibited')
# adjustment_factors row: region REG-CA-073 -> REG-CA-037, material, 2.00, source_id='SRC-PROH', review_status='validated'; the board observation is re-labelled REG-CA-073
run(db, use_region_factors=True)                 # complete; board unit price 0.80 (= 0.40 x 2.00), warnings REGION_FACTOR_APPLIED
suggested_fix: Call the shared usability test on the factor row (and its source) in _region_factor and _adjust_factors; also pick the best factor deterministically (latest valid_from) instead of table order.

summary: Region ranking is computed but not used for ranking. rank only decides accept/reject; with allow_ancestor_region_prices=True the newest observation wins regardless of specificity, so a newer state-level price silently overrides an exact-region price; an ancestor-region price carries no flag and the line input does not record region/zip/store (labor has RATE_FROM_ANCESTOR_REGION, materials have no equivalent). A sub-region observation counts as rank 0 for a parent target (documented, but not visible on the line). Latest-selection compares str(retrieved_at) (mixed offsets mis-order) and ties are broken by table order.
reproduction:
S.add_obs(db,'TEST-OBS-STATE','TEST-PRD-BOARDA','16.00',32,'SF',region='REG-US-CA',observed=date(2026,10,1))   # 0.50/SF, newer, ancestor of LA
mat(run(db, allow_ancestor_region_prices=True))['unit_cost']      # 0.50 (local LA price is 0.40); warnings only ['RETAIL_PRICE_NOT_CONTRACTOR_COST']
mat(run(db, region_id='REG-US'))['unit_cost']                     # 0.40: an LA price silently serves a national (REG-US) request
suggested_fix: Sort candidates by (rank asc, observed_at desc, retrieved_at desc as parsed datetime, observation_id); add PRICE_FROM_ANCESTOR_REGION:<id> and PRICE_FROM_SUBREGION flags; store region_id, zip, store_ref, retrieved_at, sales_tax/delivery flags in the line input.

summary: labor_rate() chooses by (region rank, effective_from) only. labor_rates.apprentice, wage_basis (overtime_1_5x/2x), project_type (building/residential/heavy/highway), classification_raw and use_context are never consulted; 'prevailing_wage' and 'federal_wage_determination' are merged and the later effective_from wins whatever the regime. A DIR/SAM determination file will contain apprentice steps and overtime-group rows for every craft, so the journeyman straight-time rate is picked by luck.
reproduction:
# three stat_wage rows, TR-DRYW, same region and statistic: 30.00 (journeyman, straight_time, 2026-05-01), 12.00 (apprentice=True, 2026-06-01), 45.00 (wage_basis='overtime_1_5x', 2026-07-01)
Engine(db).labor_rate('TR-DRYW', S.params(labor_basis='stat_loaded', annual_paid_hours=D(2080)))['components']['base_wage']   # 45
suggested_fix: Filter on apprentice=False, wage_basis='straight_time' and a required project_type; add a classification selector parameter; raise Missing('LABOR_RATE_AMBIGUOUS') when more than one candidate remains at equal rank/effective_from; keep state and federal regimes separate.

summary: A fully loaded source rate is under-costed. When includes_payroll_taxes / includes_workers_comp is true the engine skips the burden but never adds the record's own payroll_tax_hr / workers_comp_hr / other_employer_cost_hr / total_hr: only base_wage_hr (+ fringe_hr) enters the total. other_employer_cost_hr and the burden types general_liability and other can never reach a cost and are not flagged. BURDEN_PAYROLL_TAX_TYPES hard-codes five types including state_ett for every region, so an Arizona/Nevada run can never complete unless a zero-rate 'observed' row is invented.
reproduction:
# prevailing_wage row (use_context public_works_only): base 50, fringe 20, payroll_tax_hr 6, workers_comp_hr 5, other_employer_cost_hr 3, total_hr 84, includes_fringe/payroll_taxes/workers_comp all true
Engine(db).labor_rate('TR-DRYW', S.params(labor_basis='prevailing_loaded', project_type='public_works'))['total_hr']    # 70, not 84
# adding burden rows general_liability 2% and other $1.50/h to a complete stat_loaded rate leaves total_hr unchanged (42.33298...) and unflagged
suggested_fix: When includes_x is true use that record's x_hr (or total_hr) and fail if it is absent; cost 'other' and 'general_liability' rows or emit an explicit OMITTED_BURDEN flag; make applicable burden types region-dependent data instead of a constant.

summary: Burden selection ignores effective_from when several rows are in period (effective_to is optional) and ignores class_code. Ties go to table order, so a superseded open-ended rate can win; a trade-specific NATIONAL row beats a generic local row; workers' comp rows for different class codes are indistinguishable.
reproduction:
# 2025 Medicare 1.00% row (effective_to NULL) listed BEFORE the 2026 1.45% row, base wage $30
Engine(db).labor_rate('TR-DRYW', S.params(labor_basis='stat_loaded', annual_paid_hours=D(2080)))['components']['fica_medicare']   # 0.3000 (1.00%), correct 0.4350
suggested_fix: Score = (region rank, trade specificity, -effective_from) and raise on remaining ties; add class_code to the selection parameters for workers_comp.

summary: A requested job condition is silently dropped when a factor exists but is unusable. The code raises CONDITION_FACTOR_MISSING only if NO factor with that condition_desc exists (elif not anyhit); if one exists but is unreviewed, expired, assumed (in strict mode) or defined for another cost kind, hits is empty and the condition is ignored. methodology.md section 8 says a requested condition 'is a missing input, never silently ignored'.
reproduction:
# factor(productivity_condition, labor, 1.20, 'occupied_building') with review_status='unreviewed' | valid_to=2020-01-01 | origin='assumed' (strict)
run(db, conditions=('occupied_building',)).run['labor_cost']      # 0.550000 in all three cases (status complete; 0.66 expected or an incomplete run)
suggested_fix: If any factor with the tag exists for this kind but none is usable, raise Missing('CONDITION_FACTOR_UNUSABLE') naming the reason; model 'not applicable to this kind' explicitly instead of by absence.

summary: Quantity handling. (a) A price with qty_tier_min (e.g. a pallet/contractor-volume price) is accepted when RunParams.quantity is omitted (line 261 only filters when quantity is given); (b) quantity factors ignore valid_from/valid_to (conditions at 659-660 check them) and region, and the first matching range wins; (c) assembly_cost passes the assembly quantity to every child work item, so tier/quantity factors are chosen on the wrong quantity.
reproduction:
S.add_obs(db,'TEST-OBS-TIER','TEST-PRD-BOARDA','1.00',32,'SF',observed=date(2026,10,10)); (that observation: qty_tier_min=100000)
mat(run(db))['unit_cost']                                          # 0.03125 ($1.00 / 32 SF) although the price needs a 100,000-unit order
# quantity factor 0.90 with valid_to=2020-01-01 and RunParams(quantity=500): material_cost 0.403088 (applied)
suggested_fix: Exclude tier prices unless quantity is given and >= qty_tier_min (or flag QTY_TIER_PRICE_UNVERIFIED); apply the same validity tests to quantity factors; compute child quantity = assembly quantity x qty_per_assembly_unit.

summary: price_policy is not validated: any string other than 'median_of_latest_per_product' silently takes prices[0], i.e. the first product in table order (not the latest); the MEDIAN_OF_n_PRODUCTS flag is still emitted.
reproduction:
# two products, B observed later at 0.50/SF, A at 0.40/SF
[mat(run(db, price_policy=p))['unit_cost'] for p in ('median_of_latest_per_product','latest','bogus')]   # [0.45, 0.40, 0.40]
suggested_fix: Enumerate allowed policies, reject others in RunParams.__post_init__, implement a real 'latest' (max observed_at, retrieved_at) and flag correctly.

summary: run_id is a hash of target, parameters, calc version and only [component_id, resulting cost] of the RESOLVED lines. methodology.md says it covers 'the exact input values': it does not. The same cost from a different observation gives the same run_id (calculation_runs PK collision; build.py silently keeps the first and drops the second); two incomplete runs with different missing_inputs share an id as long as no line resolved (e.g. before/after one price was captured).
reproduction:
# db2 = clone of db where TEST-OBS-BOARDA is replaced by another store's observation of the same price
run(db).run['run_id'] == Engine(db2).unit_cost(WI,1,S.params()).run['run_id']        # True, inputs differ (TEST-OBS-BOARDA vs TEST-OBS-OTHER)
# real data, no prices vs one board price captured: both runs 'incomplete', both RUN-87e6ae280f37, missing lists differ
suggested_fix: Include in the fingerprint every input id + value (use the line inputs) and the sorted missing_inputs codes/refs; keep calc_version bound to code (git sha) so a fixed bug changes ids.

summary: with_assumptions mode crashes on an approved productivity assumption: _daily_output returns a 4-tuple on the assumption path (lines 616-618) but unit_cost unpacks 5 values (line 824) -> ValueError. The path is untested (only the waste assumption is).
reproduction:
# productivity observation unreviewed + approved assumption 'productivity:<labor component id>' = 1600 SF
run(db, mode='with_assumptions')      # ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 5, got 4)
suggested_fix: Return (daily, inputs, flags, 'assumed', None); add tests for every assumption type (productivity, price, labor_rate, equipment_rate, crew, quantity, waste, benefits, workers' comp).

summary: Assumption handling. value_text-only approved assumption (allowed by as_value_chk) crashes with decimal.InvalidOperation (D('None')); the benefits assumption treats ANY unit_id as $/h (line 460) while the workers'-comp assumption always multiplies by wages and ignores unit (line 485); no sign/range checks (waste -0.5 -> quantity 0.5; waste 5 -> 6.0x; a zero productivity assumption would divide by zero, by reading - the path currently crashes earlier, F1-014); several approved rows for one ref -> first wins silently; assumptions.review_status ignored; approved_by may equal proposed_by.
reproduction:
# approved waste assumption applies_to_ref='waste:<component_id>': value_text='ten percent', value_numeric NULL -> run(db, mode='with_assumptions') raises decimal.InvalidOperation
# value_numeric=-0.5 -> complete, material qty 0.5 ; value_numeric=5 -> complete, qty 6.0 ; two approved rows (0.1, 0.9) -> first wins
suggested_fix: Validate assumption type/unit/range on read (units conversion like prices), require value_numeric for numeric uses, uniqueness of approved assumption per ref, approved_by <> proposed_by, expiry required, review_status honoured.

summary: Equipment omissions. (a) fuel_cost_hr is never added: rate with fuel_included=False and fuel_cost_hr present is costed without fuel and without a flag (FUEL_NOT_PRICED only when fuel_cost_hr is NULL, line 521); (b) min_rental_period and delivery_pickup_cost are never priced (static flag only); (c) an 'equipment' component whose crew has no equipment member prices to 0 with origin 'observed' and no warning; (d) operator double count is detected only via the self-declared crew_members.is_operator flag (a TR-OPR labor member with is_operator=false plus an operator-included rate passes silently); OPERATOR_NOT_PRICED is only a flag; (e) (by reading) rental_day charges one day rate per crew-shift regardless of shifts needed.
reproduction:
# rental 25/h, fuel_included=False, fuel_cost_hr=9, delivery 75, min rental '4 hours', crew 1x PTROWEL:  equipment unit_cost 0.1000 (= 25*8/2000); fuel 9*8/2000 = 0.036 absent; warnings ['EQUIPMENT_DELIVERY_AND_MOBILIZATION_EXCLUDED']
# WI-CON-001 with a crew that has labor members only: equipment line unit_cost 0, origin 'observed', warnings []
# crew [TR-CEM x2, TR-OPR x1 (is_operator False), PTROWEL] + rate operator_included=True: no OPERATOR_DOUBLE_COUNT
suggested_fix: Add fuel_cost_hr when fuel_included is false (or fail when unknown); price or fail on min rental/delivery when flagged; raise CREW_NO_EQUIPMENT for an equipment component without equipment members; detect operator labor by trade_code (TR-OPR) as well; treat OPERATOR_NOT_PRICED/FUEL_NOT_PRICED as incomplete, not as a flag.

summary: Time-index logic. indices.applies_to is never compared with the cost kind (a LABOR index adjusts a MATERIAL price: 0.40 -> 0.60); an index is applied only when the price is older than max_price_age_days, so a 287-day-old price with time_index_id supplied is left unadjusted and unflagged; frequency 'other' is treated as annual; the index value for the as_of month is normally unpublished (PPI/ECI lag), so INDEX_VALUE_MISSING with no fallback to the latest published period; flagged index series are used (F1-002).
reproduction:
# index applies_to='labor' (values 100 -> 150), time_index_id given, board price observed 2025-06-01
mat(run(db, time_index_id='TEST-IDX-LAB'))['unit_cost']           # 0.60, 'TIME_INDEXED_PRICE'
# price observed 2026-01-10 (287 days) + time_index_id: unit_cost 0.40, no TIME_INDEXED_PRICE
suggested_fix: Require idx.applies_to in (kind,'all'); when time_index_id is supplied adjust every price whose month differs from the as_of month (store the base month used); define a documented fallback to the latest published index period with a flag.

summary: Rule 3/8 'never presented as contractor cost' is met only by a warning string. DEFAULT_CHANNELS includes retail_public, a run built from retail prices has status 'complete', mode 'strict' and a plain direct_cost_total; the same is true for a national wage used in an LA run (RATE_FROM_ANCESTOR_REGION), STALE_RATE, SALES_TAX_UNKNOWN_OR_INCLUDED, OPERATOR_NOT_PRICED. mode='strict' with min_review='unreviewed' produces a run indistinguishable (mode/status/warnings) from a validated-only run; only the parameters JSON differs.
reproduction:
r = run(db); (r.status, r.run['mode'], r.run['direct_cost_total'], r.run['warnings'])      # ('complete','strict',0.997875,['RETAIL_PRICE_NOT_CONTRACTOR_COST'])
run(db, min_review='unreviewed')                                                           # (after un-validating an observation) same shape: strict/complete, warnings only retail
suggested_fix: Add structured run columns (price_basis retail|quote|mixed, min_review, region_fallback, input_review_floor) and a status such as 'complete_proxy_basis'; make retail an explicit opt-in channel (allow_retail_proxy=True).

summary: Markup run: the PRICE (incl. overhead, contingency, profit) is stored in calculation_runs.direct_cost_total and mode is 'with_assumptions', so any consumer of 'direct_cost_total' reads a price as a direct cost; component columns are NULL. No range checks: profit_value -2 -> price -1.15, margin -0.5 accepted, overhead_pct=10 (meaning 10%) -> price 72.4; the fingerprint (line 1091) omits the basis texts, so runs differing only in stated basis share a run_id; only the first line carries inputs.
reproduction:
m = apply_markup(run(db), overhead_pct=D('0.10'), overhead_basis='b', contingency_pct=D('0.05'), contingency_basis='b', profit_method='markup', profit_value=D('0.10'), profit_basis='b')
m.run['direct_cost_total']        # 1.267800  (direct is 0.997875)
apply_markup(run(db), overhead_pct=D('10'), ..., profit_method='markup', profit_value=D('0.10'), ...).run['direct_cost_total']   # 72.445725
suggested_fix: Store price in a dedicated column (price_total) and leave direct_cost_total as the base run's direct cost; validate 0 <= pct < 1 (or require explicit ranges), margin < 1; include the basis strings and base-run line ids in the fingerprint.

summary: Rule 10 is enforced only in Python. The database accepts review_status='validated' with no reviewer, no reviewed_at and on a source whose verification_method is search_snippet_only (observations, labor rates, sources themselves); the append-only trigger lets review_status be flipped freely and keeps no review history (each flip overwrites the previous decision). promote_validated mutates in-memory rows and build.py rewrites the CSV, so the status history exists only in git.
reproduction:
update costdb.price_observations set review_status='validated' where observation_id='OBS-X1';      -- UPDATE 1 (source is search_snippet_only, reviewed_by NULL)
update costdb.sources set review_status='validated' where source_id='SRC-XSNIP';                   -- UPDATE 1 with verification_method='search_snippet_only'
suggested_fix: CHECK (review_status <> 'validated' OR (reviewed_by IS NOT NULL AND reviewed_at IS NOT NULL)); constraint trigger requiring source.verification_method='fetched_primary' for validated observed rows; add a review_events (append-only) table.

summary: Identity and 'versioned' definition tables are editable in place. products has no protection, so spec_key / content_qty / spec_attributes can be rewritten and every existing price observation silently re-maps to another spec line (v_price_history joins the live product); work_items, work_item_components, assemblies, assembly_components, crews, crew_members, adjustment_factors, assumptions can be changed without a new version (work-item quantity 0.09375 -> 99 accepted), which defeats 'links to versioned unit costs' and run reproducibility.
reproduction:
update costdb.products set spec_key='k2', content_qty=1000, content_unit_id='EA', spec_attributes='{"thickness_in":0.625}' where product_id='PRD-X1';   -- UPDATE 1; v_price_history now reports 'k2' for old observations
update costdb.work_item_components set qty_per_unit=99 where work_item_id='WI-FRM-001' and line_no=1;                                              -- UPDATE 1
suggested_fix: Apply forbid_history_rewrite (review fields/notes only) to products and to every versioned definition table; new content = new version row; add FK/trigger preventing a calc run from referencing an edited version.

summary: The material-equivalence and pack rules are not database constraints: a product with spec_key unrelated to its attributes ('garbage-key', spec_attributes {}), a product in a non-leaf category (CAT-DRY), and a price observation whose pack content differs from the product's pack (5 LB vs 32 SF) are all accepted; only validate.py (run after load) can notice.
reproduction:
insert into costdb.products (...,category_id,spec_attributes,spec_key,content_qty,content_unit_id,...) values (...,'CAT-DRY-BRD','{}','garbage-key',32,'SF',...);   -- INSERT 0 1
insert into costdb.price_observations (...,pack_content_qty,pack_content_unit_id,...) values (...,5,'LB',...);                                              -- INSERT 0 1 (product pack is 32 SF)
suggested_fix: Constraint trigger: product.category must have required_product_attributes, every required attribute present, spec_key recomputed in SQL (or generated column); observation pack (qty, unit) must equal products.content_qty/unit (or reference a pack-size table).

summary: The validator cannot see contradictions between a definition and what it prices (rules 3 and 7): a work item whose spec says '1/2 in regular board' but whose component points at the 5/8 in Type X spec_key produces 0 issues; an assembly whose spec says 5/8 Type X while its children hang 1/2 in regular produces 0 issues; cost_tags on assembly_components are never examined (the double-count control exists only for included_scope tokens and, as a warning, inside one work item).
reproduction:
# WI-DRY-001 material component re-pointed to MATS['gyp_58_x_4x8']['spec_key'] -> validate(db) == []
# ASM-WALL-001 spec_attributes['board'] = '5/8 in Type X ...' while children are WI-DRY-001 -> validate(db) == []; cost_tags=['fasteners'] on several assembly components -> []
suggested_fix: Derive a machine-checkable spec map per work item (attribute -> spec_key attribute) and compare; require assembly spec attributes to be derived from the children (or compare); turn WI_DUP_TAG into an error and extend it to assembly components.

summary: Rule 7 requires inclusions/exclusions on every assembly. included_scope is the empty array for all 10 assemblies; excluded_scope is the same four wall tokens (base_trim, corners_and_intersections, openings_headers_and_door_frames, electrical_and_mechanical_rough_in) on every assembly, including slabs, the footing and the HVAC system where they are meaningless, while the real exclusions sit only on the child work items (e.g. 11 or more child-level exclusions per assembly are not surfaced: subgrade preparation, forms, curing, gas piping, flue venting, power wiring, condensate, refrigerant charge ...). ASM-HVAC-001 is named 'Residential 3-ton split-system install' but excludes gas piping, flue, condensate, power wiring and charge; nothing on the assembly says so.
reproduction:
python3 - <<'EOF'   # (summary of data/csv/assemblies.csv)
# all 10 rows: included_scope == [] ; ASM-SLAB-001/002, ASM-FTG-001, ASM-HVAC-001 excluded_scope contains base_trim, corners_and_intersections, ...

suggested_fix: Generate assembly included_scope as the union of child included tokens and excluded_scope as child exclusions not covered by another child (plus assembly-level exclusions); add a validator rule ASM_NO_INCLUSIONS and ASM_EXCLUSION_NOT_APPLICABLE.

summary: Questionable quantity derivations (see arithmetic table): (1) drywall screws use 96/16 = 6 fasteners per 8 ft line but 48/16 + 1 = 4 lines, i.e. a fence-post +1 is applied to lines and not to fasteners per line: counting a screw at both ends gives 0.875/SF (walls, stored 0.75) and 1.125/SF (ceilings @12 in, stored 1.0); (2) R-13 batt: 1.0 SF of batt per SF of wall, but a 15 in batt in 16 in pitch consumes 15/16 = 0.9375 SF (the cavity is 14.5/16 = 0.906); (3) 'wall_height_ft: 8' with 92-5/8 in precut studs and three 1.5 in plates is a 97.125 in (8.09 ft) wall, so studs/SF (0.09375) is about 1.2% high for an 8 ft wall; (4) the scope says 'erect' but no bottom-plate-to-floor fasteners are quantified or excluded; (5) the 16d nail is hard-wired to a vinyl-coated 3-1/4 x 0.148 sinker while WI-FRM-004 explicitly says 'common'; (6) ASM-WALL-004 pairs a 10 ft steel-stud wall with WI-DRY-003, whose spec is 4x8 sheets: a 10 ft wall needs 4x10/4x12 board or horizontal hanging with butt joints and cut waste; neither the work item nor the assembly says which, and the (missing) waste factor would have to carry it; (7) WI-CON-003 describes 'two continuous bars on supports' while bar_supports_and_ties are excluded.
reproduction: arithmetic with Fractions in this report (section 'Arithmetic re-derivation')
suggested_fix: Decide and document the fence-post convention; derive batt quantity from batt width / stud pitch; add stud-length/plate stack to the spec check; add the missing fasteners or exclude them explicitly.

summary: Importer: the observation id excludes price and retrieved_at, so a same-day recapture at a different price (or a correction of a wrong entry) is dropped as a 'duplicate' and the correct value cannot be recorded in an append-only table; the price-in-evidence test is a substring test ('2.50' passes for '$12.50'); naive retrieved_at timestamps are accepted (interpreted in the server time zone by PostgreSQL); prohibited-source rows are accepted with a warning (see F1-004). bls_api.py hard-codes a personal e-mail address in the User-Agent; index_values PK allows only one vintage per day.

suggested_fix: Add price (and retrieved_at hour) to the id or add a 'supersedes_observation_id'; tokenise the price match; require tz-aware timestamps; make the contact address configuration.

summary: Protection gaps: TRUNCATE bypasses every append-only trigger (including 'TRUNCATE labor_rates CASCADE' wiping crew_members); notes is mutable on protected tables although the trigger message says only review fields; units is unprotected (to_base_num editable: SY->SF factor became 3 in v_unit_conversions), qualifier is free text (TON_FOO/'banana' accepted), base_unit_id may point to a different dimension; labor_rates has no check that total_hr equals its components or that includes_* flags agree with which component columns are filled, stat_wage may carry includes_payroll_taxes, burden_rates accepts effective_to < effective_from and wage_cap_annual on a per_hour basis; product_consumption allows coverage_qty/coats = 0; adjustment_factors allows a region factor from a region to itself and a time_index factor whose index.applies_to differs; validation_issues allows 'waived' on an error with free-text note only; assumptions allow self-approval.
reproduction: see pgtests.py results in this review (each statement returned ALLOWED).
suggested_fix: BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers; remove notes from mutable list on observation tables or add notes_history; add the missing CHECKs/triggers; restrict qualifiers to an enum and verify dimension equality.

summary: po_dates_chk uses retrieved_at::date, which depends on the session TimeZone: the same row (observed_at 2026-10-24, retrieved_at 2026-10-24T05:00:00Z) is accepted under UTC and rejected under America/Los_Angeles; validate.py and the importer use yet other date semantics. v_price_latest_validated uses DISTINCT ON (product_id, region_id): rows with NULL region (zip/store only) from different cities collapse into one 'latest', MSRP/quote/retail channels and units are not separated.
reproduction: SET timezone='America/Los_Angeles'; insert observation (observed_at '2026-10-24', retrieved_at '2026-10-24T05:00:00Z') -> violates po_dates_chk; with timezone 'UTC' accepted.
suggested_fix: Compare retrieved_at with (observed_at + 1 day) at timestamptz level or store an explicit retrieval date; add channel/unit/region-NOT-NULL conditions to the view or drop it.

summary: norm_attr_value quirks: Decimal accepts underscores so '5_8' normalises to '58' (different specs share a key); 'NaN'/'nan' raise TypeError instead of SpecError; fractions and decimals never merge ('15/32' vs 0.46875) so a correctly captured SKU can miss its target (false negative). make_id keeps 40 bits of SHA-1: on collision the importer treats a different observation as a duplicate (skipped) or merges two products with equal spec/pack.
reproduction: norm_attr_value('5_8') == '58'; norm_attr_value('NaN') -> TypeError: bad operand type for abs(): 'str'
suggested_fix: Reject non-numeric forms explicitly (regex), normalise fractions, use >= 16 hex chars or detect collisions against the natural key.

summary: calc_version is the static string 'costdb-calc/0.1.0' and every stored run has code_ref NULL (Engine(db, code_ref=None)), so a run does not identify the code that produced it; bugs fixed in calc.py do not change run ids.
reproduction: data/csv/calculation_runs.csv: calc_version 'costdb-calc/0.1.0', code_ref empty on all 35 runs.
suggested_fix: Set code_ref to the git sha (or hash of calc.py) at build; include it in the fingerprint.

summary: Person-hours per unit on the labor line is crew_size x shift / daily output and ignores crew_members.hours_per_shift, while the cost uses member hours: a laborer working 10 h on an 8 h shift costs 0.5875/SF but is reported as 0.015 person-h/SF (true 0.01625).
reproduction: crew [TR-DRYW x2 8 h, TR-LAB x1 hours_per_shift=10], norm 1600 SF/shift: labor_cost 0.5875, labor line quantity 0.0150000000
suggested_fix: Sum qty x hours over labor members for person-hours; keep crew-hours separate.

summary: Rule 4 separation of overhead/profit: company_actual rates return total_hr regardless of the includes_* flags and the schema has no includes_overhead / includes_profit flag, so a billing-type company rate can be loaded and then marked up again by apply_markup. suggested_fix: Add includes_overhead/includes_profit (must be false for use as a cost) and copy region/period from the governing input.
